passages.title: Saving Water in San Isidro
passages.text:
Two summers ago, the town of San Isidro faced a serious water shortage. Its main reservoir dropped to a third of its usual level, and some barangays received water for only four hours a day.

Instead of waiting for the rains, the municipal government launched a conservation drive. Households were given free faucet aerators, which cut water use without lowering pressure. Schools held short lessons on fixing leaks, and the public market adopted a rule that stalls must wash produce in basins instead of under running taps.

Within a year, daily water use in the town fell by nearly a fifth. Officials admit that the rains eventually helped, but they point out that the reservoir recovered faster than in earlier droughts. They now plan to make the drive a permanent program rather than an emergency measure.

passages.title: The Library After Dark
passages.text:
When the city library extended its hours until nine in the evening, many staff members expected the new schedule to fail. Few people, they argued, would come to read after dark. The first month seemed to prove them right: the reading room was nearly empty after six.

The head librarian, however, noticed that the few evening visitors were mostly working students and employees who could not come during the day. She asked them what would help. Their answers were simple: a quieter study area, more power outlets for laptops, and a way to borrow books without lining up.

The library rearranged its tables, added outlets along one wall and set up a self-checkout desk. By the sixth month, evening visits had more than tripled, and the extended hours were made official.

passages.title: Ang Diwa ng Bayanihan
passages.text:
Sa maraming baryo noon, kapag lilipat ng tirahan ang isang pamilya, tinutulungan sila ng mga kapitbahay na buhatin ang buong bahay kubo. Ito ang kilalang larawan ng bayanihan.

Bagaman bihira na itong makita ngayon, hindi nawawala ang diwa nito. Makikita pa rin ito tuwing may bagyo o baha, kapag nagtutulungan ang mga tao sa pagluluto ng pagkain, paglilinis ng mga kalsada at pagbibigay ng damit sa mga nasalanta.

Ayon sa ilang guro, ang bayanihan ay hindi lamang tungkol sa lakas ng katawan kundi sa pagkukusa. Walang nag-uutos sa mga tumutulong; kusa silang lumalapit dahil itinuturing nilang kapamilya ang kanilang kapwa.

passages.title: Memo: New Supply Requests
passages.text:
To all personnel:

Beginning next month, requests for office supplies must be submitted through the online request form instead of on paper. Requests received by Wednesday will be delivered on Friday of the same week; requests received after Wednesday will be delivered on Friday of the following week.

Urgent requests may still be made by phone to the Supply Section, but these are limited to items needed to continue a task already in progress. Paper forms will be accepted until the end of this month only.

Please direct questions about the new system to the Supply Section.

passages.title: A Buddy for Every New Hire
passages.text:
Last year, the provincial assessor's office noticed a worrying pattern. Nearly one in four new employees left within their first six months, and exit interviews showed a common complaint: newcomers felt lost and were afraid to ask questions that might seem foolish.

To address this, the office started a buddy program. Each new hire is paired with a volunteer who has served at least three years. For the first three months, the pair meets for thirty minutes every week. The buddy explains unwritten office practices, introduces the newcomer to staff in other sections and reviews the newcomer's first property assessments before they are forwarded to the supervisor.

The volunteers receive no extra pay, but their mentoring hours are counted toward their annual training requirement. Some senior staff were skeptical at first, worrying that the weekly meetings would slow down their own work.

Twelve months later, only two of the eighteen employees hired under the program had resigned. Supervisors also reported fewer errors in early assessments. The office has since shared its guidelines with three neighboring municipalities that are facing the same problem.

passages.title: Ang Halamanan sa Bakanteng Lote
passages.text:
Dati, tambakan ng basura ang bakanteng lote sa tabi ng kapilya ng Barangay Maligaya. Madalas itong pagmulan ng masamang amoy at pinamumugaran pa ng daga, kaya iniiwasan ito ng mga dumaraan.

Noong isang taon, nagkasundo ang mga opisyal ng barangay at ang samahan ng kababaihan na gawing halamanan ang lote. Nilinis ito ng mga residente tuwing Sabado, at nagbigay ng libreng binhi ang tanggapan ng agrikultura ng munisipyo. Pechay, talong, okra at kamatis ang kanilang itinanim. Ang mga balat at tirang dahon ng gulay mula sa mga kusina ay ginagawa namang pataba sa halip na itapon.

Hindi nagtagal, umani na ang halamanan. Ang bahagi ng ani ay ipinamamahagi sa mga pamilyang nangangailangan, at ang natitira ay ipinagbibili sa murang halaga. Ang kinikita naman ay ginagamit sa pagbili ng mga kagamitan at binhi para sa susunod na taniman.

Ngayon, hindi na iniiwasan ang lote. Sa halip, dinarayo na ito ng mga batang nais matutong magtanim, at ilang kalapit na barangay na ang humihingi ng payo kung paano sisimulan ang sarili nilang halamanan.

passages.title: No More Dawn Lines at the Permit Office
passages.text:
Every January, the business permit office of Dalisay City used to open its doors to lines that stretched past the parking lot. Applicants arrived before dawn, and many waited six hours only to learn that a missing document meant coming back another day.

This year, the city tried a different approach. Applicants now reserve a time slot through the city's website or at a kiosk in their barangay hall. When they book, the system lists the documents required for their type of business, so they can complete their papers before they arrive. A text message reminds them the day before their schedule.

Walk-in applicants are still served, but only after those with reservations, and two windows are set aside for senior citizens and persons with disabilities.

The results were noticeable. The average waiting time dropped from six hours to under forty minutes, and far fewer applicants were turned away for incomplete papers. Some older business owners complained at first that they did not know how to use the website, so the city assigned staff at each barangay kiosk to book slots for them. Officials say the system will be extended to building permits next year.

passages.title: Advisory: Before the Rains Come
passages.text:
ADVISORY FROM THE MUNICIPAL HEALTH OFFICE

With the rainy season expected to begin next month, residents are reminded that dengue cases in our town usually rise from June to September. The mosquito that carries the virus does not breed in rivers or swamps. It lays its eggs in clean, still water, often in containers found around the home.

All households are asked to do a ten-minute search every Saturday morning. Empty and scrub flower vases, pails and water drums, and cover any container that must store water. Throw away old tires, cans and coconut shells, or turn them upside down so they cannot collect rain. Clear roof gutters of leaves that block the flow of water.

Fogging will be done only in areas where cases have been confirmed, since spraying kills adult mosquitoes but not the eggs and larvae left in containers. Removing breeding sites remains the most effective protection.

Anyone with a high fever lasting two days or more should go to the nearest health center at once and avoid taking medicine without a doctor's advice. Consultations at all barangay health centers are free.

passages.title: Ang Klinikang Umaakyat sa Bundok
passages.text:
Sa Sitio Malinao, na nasa itaas ng bundok, tatlong oras na lakad ang layo ng pinakamalapit na health center. Dahil dito, maraming residente ang hindi nagpapatingin hangga't hindi pa malubha ang kanilang sakit.

Upang malunasan ang suliraning ito, nagsimula ang munisipyo ng isang klinikang umiikot. Tuwing ikalawang Martes ng buwan, umaakyat sa sitio ang isang doktor, dalawang nars at isang komadrona sakay ng lumang ambulansiya. Sa kapilya ng sitio sila nagtatayo ng pansamantalang klinika. Libre ang konsultasyon, ang pagkuha ng presyon at ang mga pangunahing gamot.

Hindi naging madali ang simula. Noong unang buwan, iilan lamang ang lumapit dahil hindi pa kilala ng mga residente ang mga bagong mukha. Nakipag-usap ang mga nars sa mga lider ng sitio, at ang mga lider na ito mismo ang naglibot sa mga bahay upang ipaalam ang iskedyul at ipakilala ang mga manggagamot.

Makalipas ang isang taon, halos doble na ang bilang ng mga nagpapatingin sa bawat pagbisita. Ayon sa komadrona, mas maaga na ring natutukoy ang mga buntis na nangangailangan ng espesyal na alaga.

passages.title: Paalala Tungkol sa Amilyar
passages.text:
PAALALA MULA SA TANGGAPAN NG INGAT-YAMAN NG BAYAN

Ipinapaalala sa lahat ng may-ari ng lupa at gusali na maaari nang bayaran ang amilyar (buwis sa lupa at gusali) para sa taong ito. Ang magbabayad nang buo hanggang ika-31 ng Marso ay makatatanggap ng sampung porsiyentong diskuwento. Ang hindi makapagbabayad nang buo ay maaaring magbayad nang hulugan tuwing katapusan ng bawat ikatlong buwan, ngunit wala nang diskuwento.

Ang hindi mababayaran sa takdang panahon ay papatawan ng multang dalawang porsiyento sa bawat buwan ng pagkaantala.

Upang maiwasan ang mahabang pila, bukas ang tanggapan mula ika-7 ng umaga hanggang ika-5 ng hapon, kasama ang Sabado, sa buong buwan ng Marso. Dalhin ang huling resibo ng bayad o ang numero ng tax declaration ng ari-arian. Ang magbabayad para sa ibang tao ay kailangang magdala ng sulat ng pahintulot mula sa may-ari at kopya ng ID nito.

Ang buwis na malilikom ay gagamitin sa pagpapaayos ng mga kalsada, paaralan at health center ng bayan. Para sa mga katanungan, lumapit sa Window 3 ng tanggapan.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "meticulous".
questions.explanation: Meticulous means paying very close attention to detail, which is closest to careful.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "scarce".
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply. Its opposite is abundant, which means plentiful.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Each of the applicants ___ required to submit a valid ID.
questions.explanation: The subject is "each", which is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is". "Of the applicants" does not change the subject.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The committee will meet ___ Monday ___ 9:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Use "on" for days and dates, and "at" for exact times: on Monday at 9:00 a.m.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.correct: She has worked in the agency since 2019.
wrong: She has worked in the agency since five years.
She is working in the agency since 2019.
She works in the agency since 2019.
questions.explanation: An action that started in the past and continues now takes the present perfect ("has worked"). "Since" is followed by a starting point such as 2019; a length of time uses "for".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "to burn the midnight oil" mean?
questions.correct: To work or study late into the night
wrong: To spend money carelessly on small things
To lose one's temper over something minor
To finish a task earlier than expected
questions.explanation: The idiom comes from the days of oil lamps: burning oil at midnight meant staying up late to work or study.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Despite the heavy rain, the relief operations ___ as scheduled.
questions.explanation: "Despite" signals that the operations went ahead anyway, so "proceeded" (continued) fits. "Proceeds" does not agree with the plural "operations", "proceeding" needs a helping verb such as "were", and "preceded" means came before.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Arrange the sentences into a logical paragraph.
(A) He then filled out the application form.
(B) Marco arrived at the municipal hall early.
(C) Finally, he received his claim stub.
(D) After that, he submitted the form at Window 2.
questions.explanation: B introduces Marco and the place. A ("then") follows, D ("after that") comes once the form is filled out, and C ("finally") ends the sequence.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang "masigasig"?
questions.explanation: Ang masigasig ay nangangahulugang masikap at puno ng sipag sa paggawa, kaya ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ay masipag.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Alin ang wastong pangungusap?
questions.correct: Nag-aral siya nang mabuti para sa pagsusulit.
wrong: Nag-aral siya ng mabuti para sa pagsusulit.
Nag-aral siya nang mabuti para nang pagsusulit.
Nag-aral siya ng mabuti para nang pagsusulit.
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "nang" kapag sinasagot nito ang tanong na "paano" (paano nag-aral? nang mabuti). Ang "para sa" ang wastong pang-ukol bago ang "pagsusulit".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "ubiquitous".
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous describes something found everywhere, such as mobile phones in a city.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "frugal".
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful not to waste money. Its opposite is wasteful. Thrifty is a synonym, not an opposite.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?
Neither of the two clerks / have filed / the report / before the deadline.
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular, so the verb must be singular: "Neither of the two clerks has filed the report."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The new online system was introduced to ___ the long lines at the municipal office.
questions.explanation: Alleviate means to lessen or ease. Aggravate means to make worse, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The principal's decision will greatly ___ the students.
questions.explanation: "Affect" is the verb meaning to influence. "Effect" is usually a noun meaning a result.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "to bite the bullet" mean?
questions.correct: To face a painful situation bravely
wrong: To give up before trying hard
questions.explanation: To bite the bullet is to accept something unpleasant and deal with it with courage.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Choose the sentence that best completes the paragraph.
Many government offices now accept applications online. This saves applicants a trip to the office. ___
questions.correct: As a result, the lines at service counters have become shorter.
wrong: However, the office building was completed in 1985.
Applicants must also be at least 18 years old.
The weather in the city was fine that week.
questions.explanation: The paragraph is about the benefit of online applications. Only the sentence about shorter lines continues that idea; the others change the topic.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: If I ___ the manager, I would approve the request.
questions.explanation: For an imagined situation in the present, formal English uses "were" for every subject: "If I were the manager..."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Between you and ___, the report is still incomplete.
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun: "between you and me".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The witness gave a candid account of the incident. What does "candid" mean in this sentence?
questions.explanation: A candid account is open and honest, holding nothing back.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.correct: The job requires typing, filing, and answering calls.
wrong: The job requires typing, filing, and to answer calls.
The job requires to type, filing, and answering calls.
The job requires typing, to file, and answering calls.
questions.explanation: Items in a list should have the same form. Here all three are -ing words: typing, filing, answering.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: By the time the inspector arrives, the team ___ the inventory.
questions.explanation: An action that will be complete before a future moment takes the future perfect: "will have finished".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kasalungat ng salitang "masagana"?
questions.explanation: Ang masagana ay nangangahulugang marami o sapat ang isang bagay. Ang kasalungat nito ay salat, na nangangahulugang kulang.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Piliin ang wastong salita: ___ ka ba sa pulong bukas?
questions.explanation: Ang "bukas" ay tumutukoy sa hinaharap, kaya ang wastong aspekto ay kontemplatibo: dadalo.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng sawikaing "ilaw ng tahanan"?
questions.explanation: Ang "ilaw ng tahanan" ay tumutukoy sa ina. Ang "haligi ng tahanan" naman ay ang ama.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
questions.correct: How a town reduced its water use during a shortage
wrong: Why the rains failed to come to San Isidro
How to install a faucet aerator at home
The history of the San Isidro public market
questions.explanation: Every paragraph is about the shortage and the steps the town took to use less water. The other choices are small details or are not discussed.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: According to the passage, what did the market's new rule require?
questions.correct: Washing produce in basins instead of under running taps
wrong: Closing all stalls for four hours a day
Installing a faucet aerator in every stall
Selling only produce grown in the town
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says stalls "must wash produce in basins instead of under running taps."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Why do the officials point out that the reservoir recovered faster than in earlier droughts?
questions.correct: To suggest that the conservation drive made a difference
wrong: To show that the rains were heavier than usual
To prove that the drought was not serious
To explain why the drive will be stopped
questions.explanation: Officials admit the rains helped but add that recovery was faster than before. The faster recovery is their evidence that the drive itself worked.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "permanent" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: The officials want the drive to continue "rather than" stay an emergency measure, so permanent means lasting. Temporary is its opposite.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: According to the passage, who were most of the evening visitors during the first month?
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says the evening visitors "were mostly working students and employees who could not come during the day."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What did the head librarian do that led to the change?
questions.correct: She asked the evening visitors what they needed
wrong: She shortened the library's opening hours
She hired more staff for the evening shift
She advertised the new hours on the radio
questions.explanation: The turning point is that she "asked them what would help", and the library then made the changes they suggested.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Which statement best describes what the staff expected at first?
questions.correct: They doubted that people would use the library at night
wrong: They believed evening visits would quickly triple
They wanted the library to open earlier instead
They expected the reading room to run out of seats
questions.explanation: The staff "expected the new schedule to fail" because they thought few people would come after dark.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.correct: Listening to users can turn a struggling service around
wrong: Libraries should close early to save money
New schedules usually fail in their first month
questions.explanation: Visits tripled only after the librarian asked users what they needed and acted on it. The other choices either take one detail too far or are not in the passage.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing ideya ng talata?
questions.correct: Buhay pa rin ang diwa ng bayanihan sa kasalukuyan
wrong: Hindi na ginagawa ang bayanihan sa kasalukuyan
Mahirap buhatin ang isang bahay kubo
Ang mga guro ang nag-uutos ng bayanihan
questions.explanation: Sinasabi ng talata na bihira na ang pagbubuhat ng bahay pero "hindi nawawala ang diwa nito", at nagbibigay ito ng mga halimbawa sa kasalukuyan.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ayon sa talata, kailan pa rin makikita ang bayanihan ngayon?
questions.explanation: Tahasang sinasabi ng ikalawang talata na makikita pa rin ito "tuwing may bagyo o baha".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng "pagkukusa" sa talata?
questions.explanation: Ipinaliwanag mismo ng talata: "Walang nag-uutos sa mga tumutulong; kusa silang lumalapit."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Bakit kusang tumutulong ang mga tao ayon sa talata?
questions.correct: Itinuturing nilang kapamilya ang kanilang kapwa
questions.explanation: Ang huling pangungusap ang sagot: lumalapit sila "dahil itinuturing nilang kapamilya ang kanilang kapwa".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What is the main purpose of the memo?
questions.correct: To announce a new way of requesting office supplies
wrong: To remind staff to use fewer supplies
To introduce the new head of the Supply Section
To list supplies that are no longer available
questions.explanation: The memo explains that supply requests will move from paper to an online form, and how deliveries will work.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: A request is submitted online on a Thursday. When will it be delivered?
questions.correct: On Friday of the following week
wrong: On Friday of the same week
At the end of the month
questions.explanation: Only requests received by Wednesday arrive that Friday. Thursday is after Wednesday, so delivery is on Friday of the following week.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: According to the memo, when may a supply request be made by phone?
questions.correct: When the item is needed to continue a task already in progress
wrong: Whenever the online form is slow to load
For any request made after Wednesday
questions.explanation: Phone requests are allowed only for urgent needs, which the memo limits to "items needed to continue a task already in progress".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Until when will paper request forms be accepted?
questions.correct: Until the end of this month
wrong: Until the end of next month
questions.explanation: The memo says paper forms "will be accepted until the end of this month only".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "diligent".
questions.explanation: A diligent person works hard and carefully. Lazy and careless are opposites.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "obsolete".
questions.explanation: Something obsolete is no longer used because something newer has replaced it.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "benevolent".
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind and wanting to help others.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "ambiguous".
questions.explanation: An ambiguous statement can be understood in more than one way. Ambitious only looks similar.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "mitigate".
questions.explanation: To mitigate is to make something less severe, as in "mitigate the effects of flooding".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "pragmatic".
questions.explanation: A pragmatic person deals with things in a sensible, realistic way. Idealistic is close to the opposite.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "transparent".
questions.explanation: Transparent means you can see through it; opaque means you cannot. Clear is a synonym.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "reluctant".
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling. Hesitant is a synonym.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "augment".
questions.explanation: To augment is to increase, so its opposite is reduce.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "verbose".
questions.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed; concise means brief and to the point. Wordy is a synonym.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "affluent".
questions.explanation: Affluent means rich. Wealthy is a synonym, and fluent only sounds similar.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The list of requirements ___ posted at the entrance.
questions.explanation: The subject is "list", which is singular. "Of requirements" only describes it.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ aware of the new rule.
questions.explanation: With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Clerks" is plural, so the verb is "are".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Mathematics ___ one of the subjects in the entrance test.
questions.explanation: Mathematics ends in -s but is a singular subject, like physics and news.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The number of applicants ___ increased this year.
questions.explanation: "The number of" refers to one number, so it takes a singular verb. "A number of applicants have" would be plural.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?
She don't / know where / the files are / kept.
questions.explanation: With "she", the correct form is "doesn't": She doesn't know where the files are kept.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?
The supervisor, along with / her staff, / were / present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: The subject is "the supervisor"; "along with her staff" does not make it plural. It should be "was".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?
If he would have studied, / he would have / passed / the exam.
questions.explanation: For a past condition that did not happen, the if-clause uses "had": If he had studied, he would have passed the exam.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?
The documents / were laying / on the table / all morning.
questions.explanation: "Lay" needs an object (lay the documents down). Things that rest somewhere are "lying": The documents were lying on the table.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The office will remain closed ___ further notice.
questions.explanation: "Until further notice" means until a new announcement is made.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The applicant's ___ answers impressed the interview panel.
questions.explanation: Only a positive word fits "impressed". Articulate means clear and well expressed.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Because the instructions were ___, many applicants filled out the form incorrectly.
questions.explanation: The second half says people made mistakes, so the instructions must have been hard to follow.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Her request for leave was ___ because she did not file it on time.
questions.explanation: "Because she did not file it on time" gives a reason for a negative result, so the request was denied.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "to break the ice" mean?
questions.correct: To ease the tension at the start of a meeting or conversation
questions.explanation: People "break the ice" with a joke or friendly question so that others feel more relaxed.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "a blessing in disguise" mean?
questions.correct: Something good that at first seemed bad
wrong: A secret that is finally revealed
A reward that comes too late
questions.explanation: Example: Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise, because the bus was later stuck in a flood.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "to hit the nail on the head" mean?
questions.correct: To say exactly the right thing
questions.explanation: You hit the nail on the head when you describe a situation or problem exactly right.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: What does the idiom "to cut corners" mean?
questions.correct: To do something cheaply or carelessly to save time or money
questions.explanation: The idiom is about skipping proper steps, not about roads. "To take a shorter route" is the literal meaning.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The new rule will take ___ next month.
questions.explanation: "Effect" is the noun (a result); "take effect" means start to apply. "Affect" is usually a verb.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.correct: Fewer employees came to work today.
wrong: Less employees came to work today.
Lesser employees came to work today.
Fewer employees comes to work today.
questions.explanation: Use "fewer" with things you can count (employees) and "less" with amounts (less time, less water).

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The agency updated ___ website last week.
questions.explanation: "Its" shows possession. "It's" means "it is", and "its'" is never correct.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: ___ going to submit the reports tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "They're" is short for "they are". "Their" shows possession and "there" refers to a place.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Honesty is a basic ___ of public service.
questions.explanation: A principle is a rule or belief. A principal is the head of a school or the main amount of a loan.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Maria and ___ will attend the seminar tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject, so use the subject form "I". Remove "Maria and" to check: "I will attend", not "me will attend".

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: ___ is responsible for the missing files?
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of the verb "is". "Whom" is used only as an object, as in "To whom should I send it?"

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: She has been working in the agency ___ five years.
questions.explanation: Use "for" with a length of time (for five years) and "since" with a starting point (since 2021).

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: The new clerk is not yet familiar ___ the filing system.
questions.explanation: The usual expression is "familiar with" something.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang "mapagpakumbaba"?
questions.explanation: Ang mapagpakumbaba ay hindi nagmamataas o nagyayabang, kaya mababang-loob. Kasalungat nito ang mayabang.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang "dalubhasa"?
questions.explanation: Ang dalubhasa ay taong may malawak na kaalaman o kasanayan sa isang larangan. Kasalungat nito ang baguhan.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kasalungat ng salitang "matayog"?
questions.explanation: Ang matayog ay napakataas, kaya mababa ang kasalungat. Ang mataas ay kasingkahulugan.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang kasalungat ng salitang "masinop"?
questions.explanation: Ang masinop ay maayos at maingat sa gamit at gastos. Ang burara ay pabaya at magulo sa gamit.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng sawikaing "balat-sibuyas"?
questions.explanation: Kasingnipis ng balat ng sibuyas ang pakiramdam ng taong balat-sibuyas: madali siyang masaktan o magtampo.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng sawikaing "nagbibilang ng poste"?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ito para sa taong walang hanapbuhay, na parang palakad-lakad lamang sa kalsada at nagbibilang ng poste.

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Alin ang wastong pangungusap?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "din" pagkatapos ng katinig (masipag), at ang "rin" pagkatapos ng patinig o ng w at y (pupunta, bahay). Kaya ang tamang anyo ng iba ay "Pupunta rin ako bukas" at "Bahay rin namin ito."

questions.subject: Verbal Ability
questions.question: Alin ang wastong pangungusap?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "mayroon" kapag panghalip (siya) ang kasunod. Ang "may" ay ginagamit kapag pangngalan, pandiwa o pang-uri ang kasunod, gaya ng "May bago siyang sasakyan."

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 20% of 350?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 3/4 + 2/3?
questions.explanation: Use 12 as the common denominator: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12. 9/12 + 8/12 = 17/12, which is 1 5/12.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The ratio of men to women in an office is 3:5. If there are 40 employees in all, how many are women?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 3 + 5 = 8 parts. Each part is 40 / 8 = 5 employees. Women are 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An item priced at ₱1,200 is sold at a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: The discount is 0.15 × 1,200 = 180. The selling price is 1,200 - 180 = ₱1,020.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the average of 82, 76, 90 and 88?
questions.explanation: Add the numbers: 82 + 76 + 90 + 88 = 336. Divide by how many there are: 336 / 4 = 84.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 3x - 7 = 20, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: 3x = 27. Divide both sides by 3: x = 9.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Six workers can finish a job in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how many days will nine workers need?
questions.explanation: The job takes 6 × 12 = 72 worker-days. With nine workers: 72 / 9 = 8 days. More workers means fewer days.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A bus travels at 60 kilometers per hour for 2.5 hours. How far does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance = rate × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How much simple interest does ₱10,000 earn in 3 years at 6% per year?
questions.explanation: Interest = principal × rate × time = 10,000 × 0.06 × 3 = ₱1,800. ₱11,800 is the total amount, not the interest.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the value of 8 + 12 ÷ 4 × 3 - 5?
questions.explanation: Do division and multiplication first, left to right: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 3 × 3 = 9. Then add and subtract: 8 + 9 - 5 = 12.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 3, 6, 12, 24, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is double the one before it, so 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 5, 8, 13, 20, 29, ...
questions.explanation: The gaps are 3, 5, 7 and 9, growing by 2 each time. The next gap is 11, so 29 + 11 = 40.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Ana can paint a room in 6 hours. Ben can paint the same room in 3 hours. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: Together they paint 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 of the room per hour, so the whole room takes 2 hours.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Maria is 3 times as old as her son. In 12 years, she will be twice as old as her son. How old is Maria now?
questions.explanation: Let the son be s, so Maria is 3s. In 12 years: 3s + 12 = 2(s + 12), so 3s + 12 = 2s + 24 and s = 12. Maria is 3 × 12 = 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How many liters of a 20% salt solution must be mixed with 10 liters of a 50% salt solution to make a 30% salt solution?
questions.explanation: Salt before = salt after: 0.20x + 0.50(10) = 0.30(x + 10). So 0.20x + 5 = 0.30x + 3, which gives 0.10x = 2 and x = 20.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The price of an item rose by 20% and then fell by 20%. What is the overall change from the original price?
questions.explanation: Take ₱100: after a 20% rise it is ₱120; after a 20% fall it is 120 × 0.80 = ₱96. That is ₱4 less, a 4% decrease.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: ₱10,000 is deposited at 10% interest compounded yearly. How much is in the account after 2 years?
questions.explanation: After year 1: 10,000 × 1.10 = 11,000. After year 2: 11,000 × 1.10 = 12,100. Compounding earns interest on the interest too, so it is more than ₱12,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A car travels 180 km to a town at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 90 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
questions.explanation: Going takes 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours; returning takes 180 ÷ 90 = 2 hours. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 360 ÷ 5 = 72 km/h, not the simple average of 75.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: ₱24,000 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2:3:5. How much does C receive?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 parts, so each part is ₱2,400. C gets 5 parts: 5 × 2,400 = ₱12,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Eight encoders can encode 240 forms in 5 hours. At the same rate, how many forms can 6 encoders encode in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: One encoder does 240 ÷ (8 × 5) = 6 forms per hour. Six encoders for 4 hours: 6 × 6 × 4 = 144 forms.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. What is the largest of the three?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be x, x + 2 and x + 4. Then 3x + 6 = 78, so x = 24. The numbers are 24, 26 and 28.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A ₱2,000 item is marked down 10%, and then a further 5% is taken off the new price. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After 10% off: 2,000 × 0.90 = 1,800. After a further 5% off: 1,800 × 0.95 = ₱1,710. Two discounts in a row are less than 15% off.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A worker spends 1/4 of his salary on rent and 1/3 of what is left on food. He has ₱9,000 remaining. What is his salary?
questions.explanation: After rent, 3/4 of the salary is left. Food takes 1/3 of that, which is 1/4 of the salary. What remains is 3/4 − 1/4 = 1/2 of the salary, so the salary is 2 × 9,000 = ₱18,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, ...
questions.explanation: The gaps double each time: 1, 2, 4, 8, so the next gap is 16 and 17 + 16 = 33.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 81, 27, 9, 3, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before it divided by 3, so 3 ÷ 3 = 1. (1/3 would come after 1.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 50 and their difference is 14. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: The larger number is (sum + difference) ÷ 2 = (50 + 14) ÷ 2 = 32. The smaller is 50 − 32 = 18.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An office has 80 employees, and 35% of them are men. How many are women?
questions.explanation: Men: 0.35 × 80 = 28. Women: 80 − 28 = 52. (28 is the number of men.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A rectangular lot measures 25 meters by 40 meters. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 25 × 40 = 1,000 square meters. (130 meters is the perimeter.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 4 hours, and a drain empties the full tank in 6 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Each hour the tank gains 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 of its volume, so it fills in 12 hours.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A store buys an item for ₱800 and sells it for ₱1,000. What is the profit as a percent of the cost?
questions.explanation: The profit is ₱200. As a percent of the cost: 200 ÷ 800 = 0.25, or 25%. (20% is the profit as a percent of the selling price.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average of five numbers is 18. Four of them are 15, 20, 12 and 25. What is the fifth number?
questions.explanation: The five numbers add up to 5 × 18 = 90. The four known numbers add up to 72, so the fifth is 90 − 72 = 18.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An employee works from 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. with a one-hour lunch break. How long does she actually work?
questions.explanation: From 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. is 8 hours 30 minutes. Minus the one-hour break, she works 7 hours 30 minutes.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 15% of 840?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What percent of 250 is 40?
questions.explanation: Divide the part by the whole: 40 ÷ 250 = 0.16, which is 16%.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A clerk processed 120 forms on Monday, which is 80% of the daily target. What is the daily target?
questions.explanation: 120 is 80% of the target, so the target is 120 ÷ 0.80 = 150. Taking 80% of 120 (96) answers a different question.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 5/6 − 1/4?
questions.explanation: Use 12 as the common denominator: 10/12 − 3/12 = 7/12.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 2 1/3 × 1 1/2?
questions.explanation: Change to improper fractions: 7/3 × 3/2 = 21/6 = 7/2 = 3 1/2.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 3/5 ÷ 9/10?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the reciprocal: 3/5 × 10/9 = 30/45 = 2/3.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 0.25 × 0.4?
questions.explanation: 25 × 4 = 100, and the factors have 3 decimal places in all, so the answer is 0.100 = 0.1.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 4.5 + 0.75 − 1.2?
questions.explanation: 4.5 + 0.75 = 5.25, and 5.25 − 1.2 = 4.05. Line up the decimal points when adding and subtracting.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A recipe uses 3 cups of rice for every 5 cups of water. How many cups of water are needed for 12 cups of rice?
questions.explanation: 12 cups of rice is 4 times 3 cups, so the water is 4 × 5 = 20 cups.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 4:5. If there are 20 girls, how many students are in the class?
questions.explanation: Each part is 20 ÷ 5 = 4 students, so there are 4 × 4 = 16 boys and 16 + 20 = 36 students. 16 is only the boys.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A supply of rice lasts 30 days for 12 people. At the same rate, how many days will it last for 18 people?
questions.explanation: More people finish the rice sooner (inverse proportion): 30 × 12 = 360 person-days, and 360 ÷ 18 = 20 days.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A bag sells for ₱1,350 after a 25% discount. What was its original price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 75% of the original, so the original is ₱1,350 ÷ 0.75 = ₱1,800. Adding 25% to ₱1,350 (₱1,687.50) is a common mistake.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A store buys an electric fan for ₱1,500 and marks it up by 40%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: The markup is 40% of ₱1,500 = ₱600, so the selling price is ₱1,500 + ₱600 = ₱2,100.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A phone bought for ₱8,000 is sold at a 15% loss. What is the selling price?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: At what yearly simple interest rate will ₱5,000 earn ₱900 in 3 years?
questions.explanation: Rate = interest ÷ (principal × time) = 900 ÷ (5,000 × 3) = 0.06, or 6% a year. 18% is the total for all 3 years.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How much must be invested at 8% simple interest per year to earn ₱1,200 in 2 years?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A student's average in four tests is 85. What score must the student get in the fifth test to raise the average to 87?
questions.explanation: Five tests averaging 87 total 435. The first four total 4 × 85 = 340, so the fifth must be 435 − 340 = 95.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average age of 5 employees is 30. When a new employee joins, the average becomes 31. How old is the new employee?
questions.explanation: The total goes from 5 × 30 = 150 to 6 × 31 = 186, so the new employee is 186 − 150 = 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: In an office, 10 employees earn an average of ₱20,000 a month and 15 employees earn an average of ₱25,000. What is the average monthly salary of all 25?
questions.explanation: Total pay is 10 × ₱20,000 + 15 × ₱25,000 = ₱575,000, and ₱575,000 ÷ 25 = ₱23,000. Simply averaging ₱20,000 and ₱25,000 ignores that the groups are different sizes.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 5x + 8 = 3x + 20, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 3x and 8 from both sides: 2x = 12, so x = 6.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If x/4 + 3 = 11, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 3: x/4 = 8. Multiply by 4: x = 32.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Seven less than twice a number is 25. What is the number?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Adult tickets cost ₱150 and child tickets cost ₱90. A group paid ₱1,380 for 12 tickets. How many adult tickets did they buy?
questions.explanation: If all 12 were child tickets, the cost would be ₱1,080. Each adult ticket adds ₱60, and ₱1,380 − ₱1,080 = ₱300, so there are 300 ÷ 60 = 5 adult tickets.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A cashier has only ₱20 and ₱50 bills: 30 bills worth ₱1,140 in all. How many ₱50 bills are there?
questions.explanation: If all 30 were ₱20 bills, they would be worth ₱600. Each ₱50 bill adds ₱30, and ₱1,140 − ₱600 = ₱540, so there are 540 ÷ 30 = 18 ₱50 bills. 12 is the number of ₱20 bills.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Paolo is 6 years older than Carla. The sum of their ages is 44. How old is Paolo?
questions.explanation: Carla is c and Paolo is c + 6, so 2c + 6 = 44 and c = 19. Paolo is 19 + 6 = 25.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Five years ago, a father was 4 times as old as his son. Today the sum of their ages is 60. How old is the son today?
questions.explanation: Five years ago their ages added up to 60 − 10 = 50, split 4:1, so the son was 10. Today he is 10 + 5 = 15.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Ana can finish a report in 4 days and Ben can finish it in 12 days. Working together, how many days will they need?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/4 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3 of the report a day, so they need 3 days.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Two printers together finish a print job in 6 hours. One printer alone takes 10 hours. How long would the other printer take alone?
questions.explanation: The other printer does 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15 of the job an hour, so it needs 15 hours alone.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A jeepney covers 45 km in 1 hour 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: 1 hour 30 minutes is 1.5 hours, and 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Two cars leave the same point at the same time and drive in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. How far apart are they after 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Going in opposite directions, the gap grows by 50 + 70 = 120 km every hour, so after 3 hours it is 360 km.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A van leaves a terminal at 8:00 a.m. traveling at 40 km/h. A car leaves the same terminal at 9:00 a.m. on the same road at 60 km/h. At what time does the car catch up with the van?
questions.explanation: By 9:00 the van is 40 km ahead. The car gains 60 − 40 = 20 km each hour, so it needs 2 hours and catches up at 11:00 a.m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 7, 11, 15, 19, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 19 + 4 = 23.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...
questions.explanation: These are the squares 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so the next is 6² = 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ...
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 3, 5, 10, 12, 24, 26, ...
questions.explanation: The steps alternate between "add 2" and "multiply by 2": 3 +2 = 5, ×2 = 10, +2 = 12, ×2 = 24, +2 = 26, so next is 26 × 2 = 52.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What number comes next? 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the missing number? 100, 95, 85, 70, __, 25
questions.explanation: The amounts subtracted grow by 5: −5, −10, −15, −20, −25. So 70 − 20 = 50, and 50 − 25 = 25 checks.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the value of 18 ÷ 3 + 4 × 5?
questions.explanation: Divide and multiply before adding: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 and 4 × 5 = 20, then 6 + 20 = 26. Working left to right without the rule gives 50.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the value of (12 − 4)² ÷ 4 + 3?
questions.explanation: Parentheses first: 12 − 4 = 8. Then the exponent: 8² = 64. Then 64 ÷ 4 = 16, and 16 + 3 = 19.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is √144 + 2³?
questions.explanation: √144 = 12 and 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so the sum is 20. Reading 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6 gives 18.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A square has a perimeter of 48 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Each side is 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm, so the area is 12 × 12 = 144 square cm.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A circular garden has a radius of 14 meters. Using π = 22/7, what is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 14 = 88 m. 616 is the area in square meters, and 44 m uses the radius in place of the diameter.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A water tank is 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1 m high. How many liters does it hold when full? (1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters)
questions.explanation: Volume = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 cubic meters, and 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 liters.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Enrollment in a school rose from 1,250 to 1,500. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 250, and percent change is measured from the old value: 250 ÷ 1,250 = 20%. Dividing by the new value gives 16 2/3%.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A town's population fell from 40,000 to 34,000. What is the percent decrease?
questions.explanation: The drop is 6,000, and 6,000 ÷ 40,000 = 0.15, a 15% decrease. 85% is what remains, not the decrease.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A seminar starts at 1:40 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 35 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.explanation: 1:40 + 2 hours = 3:40. Adding 35 minutes: 20 minutes reaches 4:00 and 15 more makes 4:15 p.m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If March 1 falls on a Monday, what day of the week is March 25?
questions.explanation: March 25 is 24 days after March 1. 24 = 3 weeks and 3 days, so it is 3 days after Monday: Thursday.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How many minutes are there in 3.75 hours?
questions.explanation: 3.75 × 60 = 225 minutes (3 hours = 180 minutes, and 0.75 hour = 45 minutes).

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A ribbon is 2.4 meters long. How many 30-centimeter pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: 2.4 meters is 240 cm, and 240 ÷ 30 = 8 pieces. Change both lengths to the same unit first.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How many liters of pure water must be added to 12 liters of a 30% alcohol solution to make a 20% solution?
questions.explanation: The solution holds 0.30 × 12 = 3.6 liters of alcohol. For that to be 20%, the total must be 3.6 ÷ 0.20 = 18 liters, so add 18 − 12 = 6 liters of water.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Coffee worth ₱400 per kg is mixed with coffee worth ₱250 per kg to make 30 kg of a blend worth ₱300 per kg. How many kilograms of the ₱400 coffee are used?
questions.explanation: Let a be the kilograms of ₱400 coffee: 400a + 250(30 − a) = 300 × 30. This gives 150a + 7,500 = 9,000, so a = 10.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 105. What is the smallest of the three?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 105 ÷ 3 = 35, so the three numbers are 33, 35 and 37. The smallest is 33.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A ₱45,000 bonus is shared by two employees in the ratio 4:5. How much more is the larger share than the smaller share?
questions.explanation: There are 9 parts of ₱45,000 ÷ 9 = ₱5,000 each. The shares are ₱20,000 and ₱25,000, so the difference is one part: ₱5,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A ₱30,000 monthly salary is raised by 10% this year and by another 10% next year. What will the salary be after both raises?
questions.explanation: After the first raise: ₱30,000 × 1.10 = ₱33,000. After the second: ₱33,000 × 1.10 = ₱36,300. The second raise is 10% of the new salary, which is why the total is more than ₱36,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Of 600 applicants, 3/5 took the exam, and 1/4 of those who took it passed. How many passed?
questions.explanation: 3/5 of 600 = 360 took the exam, and 1/4 of 360 = 90 passed. 150 is 1/4 of all applicants, not of those who took the exam.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An office budget of ₱120,000 is split as follows: 45% for salaries, 30% for supplies and the rest for travel. How much is for travel?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Three bells ring every 6, 8 and 12 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together again after the least common multiple of 6, 8 and 12, which is 24 minutes: 8:24 a.m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the greatest number of identical gift packs that can be made from 48 pens and 72 notebooks, with nothing left over?
questions.explanation: The number of packs must divide both 48 and 72. Their greatest common factor is 24, giving 24 packs of 2 pens and 3 notebooks each.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What letter comes next? A, C, F, J, ...
questions.explanation: The jumps grow by one each time: A to C is 2, C to F is 3, F to J is 4. The next jump is 5 letters after J: K, L, M, N, O.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to ___.
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital. The matching relationship for a teacher is the place of work, which is a school.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Pen is to write as knife is to ___.
questions.explanation: A pen is a tool used to write. A knife is a tool used to cut. The other choices name a quality, a part or a place, not what the knife is used to do.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: All clerks are employees. All employees have ID cards. Which conclusion must be true?
wrong: Everyone with an ID card is a clerk.
Some clerks have no ID cards.
questions.explanation: Clerks are inside the group of employees, and every employee has an ID card, so every clerk has one. The statements do not say that only clerks have ID cards.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Ana is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Carlo. Dina is shorter than Carlo. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: From tallest to shortest the order is Ana, Ben, Carlo, Dina. Dina is shorter than Carlo, who is already shorter than the other two.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which one does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Mango, banana and papaya are fruits. A carrot is a root vegetable.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If it rains, the flag ceremony is held indoors. Today the flag ceremony was held outdoors. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: Rain always moves the ceremony indoors. Since the ceremony was outdoors, there could not have been rain.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: An office processed 120 permits in January, 150 in February and 180 in March. By what percent did the number of permits increase from January to March?
questions.explanation: The increase is 180 - 120 = 60 permits. Compare it with the starting number: 60 / 120 = 0.5, or 50%.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Author is to novel as composer is to ___.
questions.explanation: An author creates a novel; a composer creates a piece of music such as a symphony.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Thermometer is to temperature as barometer is to ___.
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Ignorance is to knowledge as poverty is to ___.
questions.explanation: Ignorance is the lack of knowledge; poverty is the lack of wealth.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Some managers are lawyers. All lawyers are graduates. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.explanation: The managers who are lawyers must be graduates, so at least some managers are graduates. Nothing is said about the other managers.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: No accountants are engineers. Some engineers are teachers. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.explanation: The teachers who are engineers cannot be accountants, so some teachers are not accountants. Other teachers may or may not be accountants.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If an employee is a supervisor, she has a reserved parking slot. Liza has a reserved parking slot. What can be concluded?
questions.correct: Nothing certain can be said about whether Liza is a supervisor.
wrong: Everyone with a slot is a supervisor.
questions.explanation: The rule says supervisors have slots, not that only supervisors have them. Liza could have a slot for another reason, so nothing certain follows.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Five employees sit in a row. Ana is to the left of Ben. Carl is to the right of Ben. Dan is to the left of Ana. Eva sits between Ben and Carl. Who sits in the middle seat?
questions.explanation: The only order that fits is Dan, Ana, Ben, Eva, Carl from left to right. The middle (third) seat is Ben.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If CAT is written as DBU, how is DOG written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: C→D, A→B, T→U. So D→E, O→P, G→H gives EPH.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: A division's yearly budget is: salaries ₱500,000; supplies ₱150,000; travel ₱100,000; utilities ₱250,000. What percent of the total budget goes to salaries?

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: A division's yearly budget is: salaries ₱500,000; supplies ₱150,000; travel ₱100,000; utilities ₱250,000. Supplies and travel together are what percent of utilities?
questions.explanation: Supplies and travel add up to 150,000 + 100,000 = ₱250,000, which equals the utilities budget, so they are 100% of it.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which one does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Triangle, square and pentagon are flat (two-dimensional) shapes. A cube is a solid (three-dimensional) shape.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Rico walks 4 km north, then 3 km east. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line?
questions.explanation: His path forms a right triangle with sides 3 and 4. The straight-line distance is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km. (7 km is the distance walked.)

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Scalpel is to surgeon as gavel is to ___.
questions.explanation: A surgeon works with a scalpel; a judge uses a gavel in court.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Bird is to flock as fish is to ___.
questions.explanation: A group of birds is a flock; a group of fish is a school. Herd, pack and pride are groups of other animals.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Drought is to water as famine is to ___.
questions.explanation: A drought is a lack of water; a famine is a lack of food. Hunger is a result of famine, not what is lacking.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Chapter is to book as episode is to ___.
questions.explanation: A chapter is one part of a book; an episode is one part of a series.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Timid is to bold as cautious is to ___.
questions.explanation: Timid and bold are opposites, so the answer is the opposite of cautious. Careful means the same as cautious.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What letter comes next? B, D, G, K, P, ...
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. P is the 16th letter, and 16 + 6 = 22, which is V.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, DW, ...
questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward through the alphabet (A, B, C, D, E) while the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W, V).

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What letter comes next? Z, X, U, Q, ...
questions.explanation: The letters go back by 2, 3, 4, then 5. Q is the 17th letter, and 17 − 5 = 12, which is L.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If FILE is written as GJMF, how is DESK written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet: D→E, E→F, S→T, K→L.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a code, BOOK is written as YLLP. How is DESK written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its mirror in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X, and so on). So D→W, E→V, S→H and K→P.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a code language, "pik nar tos" means "submit the report" and "tos lem pik" means "read the report". Which word means "submit"?
questions.explanation: "pik" and "tos" appear in both phrases, so they stand for "the" and "report". The only other word in the first phrase, "nar", must mean "submit".

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: All memos are documents. Some documents are confidential. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.correct: None of these must be true.
questions.explanation: The confidential documents may or may not include memos, so neither "some memos are" nor "no memo is" can be proven. Only "none must be true" is safe.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If an applicant passes the exam, she is interviewed. If she is interviewed, she is ranked. Maria passed the exam. What must be true?
questions.explanation: Passing leads to an interview, and an interview leads to ranking, so Maria is ranked. Nothing is said about hiring or her place in the ranking.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Rule: "Only employees with an ID may enter the records room." Joel entered the records room. If the rule was followed, what must be true?
wrong: Joel works in the records room.
Everyone with an ID entered the room.
questions.explanation: "Only employees with an ID" means anyone who enters has an ID. It does not mean everyone with an ID goes in.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Each staff member takes either the morning shift or the afternoon shift, never both. Ella does not take the morning shift. What follows?
questions.explanation: There are only two choices and everyone takes one. If it is not the morning shift, it must be the afternoon shift.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a line, Rosa is 7th from the front and 12th from the back. How many people are in the line?
questions.explanation: 6 people are ahead of Rosa and 11 are behind her, so the line has 6 + 1 + 11 = 18. Adding 7 and 12 counts Rosa twice.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Four offices are on the 1st to 4th floors of a building. Accounting is above Records. HR is on the top floor. Legal is below Records. Which office is on the 2nd floor?
questions.explanation: HR takes the 4th floor. Legal is below Records and Records is below Accounting, so from the bottom: Legal (1st), Records (2nd), Accounting (3rd).

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Gina is older than Hector but younger than Ivan. Jose is older than Ivan. Karen is the youngest of the five. Who is the oldest?
questions.explanation: From oldest to youngest: Jose, Ivan, Gina, Hector, Karen.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Lito faces north. He turns right, then right again, then left. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: North, right turn → east, right turn → south, left turn → east.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: A messenger walks 6 km east, then 8 km north, then 6 km west. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The 6 km east and 6 km west cancel out, leaving him 8 km north of where he started. 20 km is the total distance walked.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Permits issued by an office: 1st quarter 240, 2nd quarter 300, 3rd quarter 180, 4th quarter 280. How many permits were issued in the whole year?

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Permits issued by an office: 1st quarter 240, 2nd quarter 300, 3rd quarter 180, 4th quarter 280. Which quarter had the biggest increase over the quarter before it?
questions.explanation: The 2nd quarter rose by 60 (240 to 300) and the 4th by 100 (180 to 280). The 3rd quarter fell, and the 1st has no earlier quarter to compare.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Permits issued by an office: 1st quarter 240, 2nd quarter 300, 3rd quarter 180, 4th quarter 280. The 3rd quarter's permits were what percent of the 2nd quarter's?
questions.explanation: 180 ÷ 300 = 0.60, or 60%. 40% is the drop, and 166 2/3% divides the other way.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which one does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Peso, yen and euro are currencies. A ledger is a book of accounts.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which number does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: 9, 25 and 49 are perfect squares (3², 5², 7²). 63 is not a perfect square.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Names are filed alphabetically by last name. Which name comes first?
questions.explanation: Compare letter by letter: "Sanc" comes before "Sant", so Sanchez is filed before Santiago and Santos.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: These names are filed alphabetically: Reyes, Carlo; Reyes, Carla; Reyes, Carmen; Reyes, Carlos. Which one is filed last?
questions.explanation: With the same last name, file by first name: Carla, Carlo, Carlos, Carmen. "Carm" comes after "Carl", and a shorter name (Carlo) comes before a longer one that starts the same (Carlos).

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Accommodate has a double c and a double m.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Necessary has one c and a double s.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: After c, the usual order is "ei": receive, ceiling, deceive.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Commission has a double m and a double s, as in Civil Service Commission.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which pair of numbers is exactly the same?
questions.explanation: Check digit by digit. In each of the other pairs, two digits have swapped places.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which pair of names is exactly the same?
questions.correct: Ma. Cristina R. Villanueva and Ma. Cristina R. Villanueva
wrong: Rodolfo T. Macaraeg and Rodolfo T. Macaraig
Josefina L. Bautista and Josefina I. Bautista
Emmanuel G. Dizon and Emmanuel C. Dizon
questions.explanation: The other pairs differ in one letter each: Macaraeg/Macaraig, middle initial L/I, and middle initial G/C.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Letters are filed by date, with the most recent first. Which of these letter dates is filed first?
questions.explanation: Most recent first means the latest date goes on top: March 12, 2026.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: File numbers 1052, 1205, 1025 and 1250 are arranged from lowest to highest. Which number is third?
questions.explanation: From lowest to highest: 1025, 1052, 1205, 1250. The third is 1205.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A caller asks to speak with an officer who is in a meeting. What should the clerk do?
questions.correct: Take a message with the caller's name, number and purpose.
wrong: Interrupt the meeting to pass the call.
Ask the caller to call again later.
Give out the officer's personal mobile number.
questions.explanation: Taking a complete message lets the officer return the call without disrupting the meeting or sharing private information.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In a business letter, where is the complimentary close, such as "Very truly yours", placed?
questions.correct: After the body, before the signature
questions.explanation: The complimentary close comes right after the last paragraph and just before the signature.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What does "cc" at the bottom of a letter mean?
questions.correct: A copy was sent to the person named
wrong: The letter was checked and corrected
questions.explanation: "cc" stands for carbon copy or courtesy copy: the people listed after it received a copy of the letter.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which filing system arranges records by place, such as region or province?
questions.explanation: A geographic system files records by location. Alphabetic uses names, numeric uses numbers, and chronological uses dates.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: An office received 125 documents on Monday, 98 on Tuesday and 142 on Wednesday. How many documents did it receive in all?

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Names are filed alphabetically by last name. Which name is filed last?
questions.explanation: The order is Yap, Zabala, Zamora, Zamudio. Zamora and Zamudio match up to "Zam"; then "u" comes after "o".

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Names are filed alphabetically. Which name is filed first?
questions.explanation: "Nothing comes before something": a name that ends sooner is filed before the same name with more after it. Cruz, Ana comes before Cruz, Ana B., and every Cruz comes before Cruzado.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Surnames with prefixes are filed as one word, ignoring spaces and capital letters. Which name is filed first?
questions.explanation: Read them as DELACRUZ, DELAROSA, DELROSARIO and DELOSSANTOS. The first two share DELA, then C comes before R, so De la Cruz is first.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In filing business names, a leading "The" is ignored. Which name is filed third?
questions.explanation: Ignoring "The", the order is Fernandez, Gamboa, Garden, Haven. "Gamboa" and "Garden" share "Ga", then "m" comes before "r".

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which pair is exactly the same?
questions.explanation: Compare character by character. The other pairs swap two digits (2217/2271, 0048/0084) or two letters (PRC/PCR).

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which pair of addresses is exactly the same?
questions.correct: 1452 Mabini St., Ermita and 1452 Mabini St., Ermita
wrong: 1452 Mabini St., Ermita and 1425 Mabini St., Ermita
1452 Mabini St., Ermita and 1452 Mabini Ave., Ermita
1452 Mabini St., Ermita and 1452 Mabimi St., Ermita
questions.explanation: Check the number, the street name and the street type. The others differ in 1452/1425, St./Ave. and Mabini/Mabimi.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question:
How many of these pairs are exactly the same?
38291 – 38291
50716 – 50176
77403 – 77403
19258 – 19285
questions.explanation: 38291 and 77403 match. 50716/50176 and 19258/19285 each have two digits swapped.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which name is exactly the same as "Bienvenido Q. Escalante"?
questions.explanation: The others change one letter: Bienv-i-nido, the middle initial O, and Escal-e-nte.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Separate has "a" in the middle: sep-a-rate. A memory aid: there is "a rat" in separate.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Occurrence has double c, double r, and ends in -ence.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The verb is maintain, but the noun drops the "ai": main-te-nance.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Questionnaire has a double n and ends in -aire.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which word is misspelled?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is liaison, with an "i" on both sides of the "a". The other three are spelled correctly.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In a business letter, which part gives the name and address of the person receiving the letter?
questions.explanation: The inside address names the receiver and their address. The heading or letterhead gives the sender's details, and the salutation is the greeting.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What does "Encl." at the bottom of a letter mean?
questions.correct: Something is included with the letter
wrong: A copy was sent to another person
questions.explanation: "Encl." stands for enclosure: a document is sent along with the letter. A copy to another person is marked "cc".

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A memorandum (memo) is mainly used for:
questions.correct: Communication within an office or agency
questions.explanation: A memo is an internal message between offices or staff of the same organization.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which document records what was discussed and decided in a meeting?
questions.explanation: The minutes are the written record of a meeting. The agenda is the list of topics prepared before it.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Before filing, a clerk marks a document with the name or number under which it will be filed. What is this step called?
questions.explanation: Coding is marking the filing caption on the document. Inspecting checks it is ready to file, sorting puts documents in order, and storing places them in the file.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What is an "OUT" guide used for in a file drawer?
questions.correct: To show that a record was taken out and who has it
wrong: To mark the end of the drawer
To separate old files from new ones
To list files to be destroyed
questions.explanation: An OUT guide replaces a borrowed record and notes who took it and when, so it can be traced and returned to the right place.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: When is a cross-reference sheet used?
questions.correct: When a record could be looked for under more than one name
wrong: When a record is borrowed from the file
When a record is due to be destroyed
When a file drawer is full
questions.explanation: A cross-reference sheet is filed under the other possible name and points to where the record is actually kept, for example a company's old and new names.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A clerk types 45 words per minute. How long will it take to type a 1,350-word report?

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: An office uses 3 reams of paper a week, and one ream has 500 sheets. How many sheets does it use in 8 weeks?
