questions.explanation: The third group reads 3365 in one and 3356 in the other.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which address is exactly the same as "Blk 9 Lot 21, Sampaguita St., Brgy. Malanday, Valenzuela City"?
questions.correct: Blk 9 Lot 21, Sampaguita St., Brgy. Malanday, Valenzuela City
wrong: Blk 9 Lot 12, Sampaguita St., Brgy. Malanday, Valenzuela City
Blk 9 Lot 21, Sampaguita Ave., Brgy. Malanday, Valenzuela City
Blk 9 Lot 21, Sampaguita St., Brgy. Malinta, Valenzuela City
questions.explanation: The others change the lot number, the street type, or the barangay.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: How many differences are there between "3/F Ayala Tower, 6750 Ayala Ave., Makati City 1226" and "3/F Ayala Tower, 6570 Ayala Ave., Makati City 1226"?
questions.explanation: Only the street number differs: 6750 and 6570.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which pair of addresses is exactly alike?
questions.correct: 45 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City / 45 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City
wrong: 45 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City / 45 Osmena Blvd., Cebu City
45 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City / 54 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City
45 Osmeña Blvd., Cebu City / 45 Osmeña St., Cebu City
questions.explanation: The other pairs differ by the ñ, the house number, or Blvd. and St.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which name is filed first? Villanueva, Rosa; Villamor, Ben; Villaflor, Ana; Villarica, Jun
questions.explanation: All start with VILLA; compare the next letter: F, M, N, R. Villaflor comes first.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which name is filed last? Santos, Maria; Santos, Mario; Santos, Mariano; Santos, Marilou
questions.explanation: With the same surname, compare given names: MARIA, MARIANO, MARILOU, MARIO. "MARIO" (O) comes after "MARIL" (L).

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Under the rule "nothing before something", which is filed first: Cruz, J.; Cruz, Jose; Cruz, Joseph; Cruz, Jo?
questions.explanation: An initial alone is shorter, so it comes before any longer name that starts with the same letter.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: How is the government office "Department of Health" usually indexed for filing?
questions.explanation: Government agencies are indexed by the distinctive word: Health, Department of.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Filing letter by letter and ignoring the hyphen, which comes first: Reyes-Lim, Carla or Reyes, Carlos?
wrong: It depends on the first names only
questions.explanation: REYES alone is shorter than REYESLIM, so "Reyes, Carlos" comes first ("nothing before something").

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: How is "Engr. Pablo Q. Ramos III" indexed?
questions.explanation: Surname first, then given name and initial; the suffix follows, and the title goes in parentheses at the end.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In straight numeric order, which file number comes third? 10452, 10425, 10524, 10245
questions.explanation: Smallest to largest: 10245, 10425, 10452, 10524. The third is 10452.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Oldest first, which date comes last? 2025-11-30, 2025-12-01, 2025-09-15, 2025-12-10
questions.explanation: Oldest to newest: September 15, November 30, December 1, December 10.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which records should usually be kept permanently?
questions.correct: Records with lasting legal or historical value, such as laws and ordinances
wrong: Daily visitor logbooks kept at the front desk
Extra photocopies of memos already filed
questions.explanation: Records with permanent legal, historical or administrative value are kept; routine and duplicate records are disposed of after their retention period.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What is the main reason for labeling folders clearly and consistently?
questions.correct: So records can be found quickly by anyone in the office
wrong: So the folders look more expensive
So only one person can use them
questions.explanation: Clear, consistent labels make records easy to find and return to the right place.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which filing system is best for the personnel records of 2,000 employees identified by employee number?
questions.explanation: When each record already has a unique number, numeric filing is fast and accurate.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A visitor arrives while you are on the phone. What should you do first?
questions.correct: Acknowledge the visitor with a nod or gesture, then finish the call
wrong: Ignore the visitor until the call ends
Ask the caller to call back tomorrow
questions.explanation: A quick acknowledgment shows courtesy to the visitor without being rude to the caller.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which item belongs in the minutes of a meeting?
questions.correct: The decisions made and who is responsible for each action
wrong: Every word said by each person
questions.explanation: Minutes record attendance, decisions, and action items, not a full transcript or opinions.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Before photocopying a confidential document, what should a clerk check first?
questions.correct: Whether they are authorized to copy and handle it
wrong: Whether the paper is the right color
Whether the copier is the newest model
Whether a co-worker wants a copy too
questions.explanation: Confidential documents may only be copied and handled by authorized staff.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What does "FIFO" mean when using office supplies?
questions.correct: First in, first out: use older stock first
wrong: File in, file out: return every file
Fast in, fast out: order supplies quickly
questions.explanation: First in, first out means older stock is used before newer stock, so nothing expires unused.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: An urgent letter must reach a regional office today. Which is the best way to send it?
questions.correct: By email or another electronic channel, with the original sent by courier
wrong: By keeping it until the next weekly mailing
By asking the recipient to visit
questions.explanation: Urgent communication should use the fastest official channel, with the original following when needed.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: What does "cc" at the bottom of a letter mean?
questions.correct: Copies of the letter were sent to the persons named
wrong: The letter needs a second signature
questions.explanation: "cc" (carbon copy, now courtesy copy) lists other people who received a copy.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In a business letter, what is the purpose of the "attention line", such as "Attention: Records Officer"?
questions.correct: To direct a letter addressed to an office to a particular person
wrong: To show the date the letter was received
To show who typed the letter
questions.explanation: The attention line routes a letter sent to an organization to the person who should act on it.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In a memorandum, what does the "Subject" or "Re" line contain?
questions.correct: A short statement of what the memo is about
wrong: The list of people who received copies
The date the memo was filed
questions.explanation: The subject line tells the reader the topic at a glance.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Which closing is the most appropriate for a formal letter to a government official?
questions.explanation: Formal letters to officials use respectful closings such as "Respectfully yours" or "Very truly yours".

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: In a business letter, what do reference initials such as "JDC:mrs" show?
questions.correct: Who wrote the letter and who typed it
wrong: The date the letter was sent
questions.explanation: The writer's initials come first, then the typist's.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A clerk works from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a one-hour lunch break, five days a week. How many hours does the clerk work in a week?
questions.explanation: Each day is 9 hours minus 1 hour of lunch = 8 hours. 8 × 5 = 40 hours.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Petty cash started at ₱5,000. Expenses were ₱1,250, ₱875 and ₱1,340. How much is left?

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: An office uses 3 reams of paper a week. One box holds 10 reams. How many boxes are needed for 20 weeks?

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: An employee earns ₱650 a day. How much is earned in 22 working days?

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: Out of 480 applications, 15% were incomplete. How many were complete?
questions.explanation: 15% of 480 = 72 incomplete. 480 − 72 = 408 complete.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A citizen needs a copy of a birth certificate. Which agency issues it?
questions.explanation: The Philippine Statistics Authority keeps civil registry records such as birth certificates.

questions.subject: Clerical Ability
questions.question: A complaint about an unregistered motor vehicle should go to which agency?
questions.explanation: The Land Transportation Office registers motor vehicles and issues licenses.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 2/3 + 5/6?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 3/4 of 120?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 7/8 − 1/3?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 4/5 ÷ 2/3?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the reciprocal: 4/5 × 3/2 = 12/10 = 1 1/5.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 3.6 × 0.25?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 12.48 ÷ 0.4?
questions.explanation: Multiply both by 10: 124.8 ÷ 4 = 31.2.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Which fraction is equal to 0.375?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An employee spends 1/4 of her salary on rent and 1/3 on food. What fraction of her salary is left?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Two-fifths of 60 employees are women. How many are men?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Juan read 1/3 of a book on Monday and half of the remaining pages on Tuesday. He still has 120 pages left. How many pages does the book have?
questions.explanation: After Monday, 2/3 is left. He reads half of that, leaving 1/3 of the book = 120 pages. The book has 360 pages.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: 18 is what percent of 72?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: 40% of what number is 64?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A restaurant bill of ₱1,200 has a 10% service charge added. What is the total?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Of 250 examinees, 64% passed. How many failed?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The price of a kilo of rice rose from ₱80 to ₱92. What was the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is ₱12. ₱12 ÷ ₱80 = 0.15, or 15%.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Applications at an office fell from 1,600 to 1,200. What was the percent decrease?
questions.explanation: The drop is 400. 400 ÷ 1,600 = 0.25, or 25%. (Dividing by 1,200 would wrongly give 33⅓%.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A salary of ₱25,000 is raised by 8%. What is the new salary?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A bag priced at ₱3,500 is sold at 30% off. What is the sale price?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: After a 15% discount, a jacket costs ₱1,360. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 85% of the original: ₱1,360 ÷ 0.85 = ₱1,600.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A store sells an item for ₱1,560, making a 30% profit on its cost. What was the cost?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 130% of the cost: ₱1,560 ÷ 1.30 = ₱1,200. (Taking 30% off ₱1,560 would wrongly give ₱1,092.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A vendor buys 50 items at ₱40 each and sells all of them at ₱52 each. What is the total profit?
questions.explanation: Profit per item is ₱12. ₱12 × 50 = ₱600.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An item was sold for ₱900 at a loss of 10% of its cost. What was the cost?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 90% of the cost: ₱900 ÷ 0.90 = ₱1,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: ₱2,700 is shared between two people in the ratio 4 : 5. How much is the larger share?
questions.explanation: There are 9 parts, so one part is ₱300. The larger share is 5 × ₱300 = ₱1,500.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: On a map with a scale of 1 : 50,000, two towns are 3 cm apart. What is the actual distance?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 5 ballpens cost ₱60, how much do 8 ballpens cost at the same price?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Six typists can finish encoding in 10 days. How many typists are needed to finish it in 4 days?
questions.explanation: The work is 6 × 10 = 60 typist-days. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 typists.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 4x − 9 = 3x + 5, what is x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 3x from both sides: x − 9 = 5, so x = 14.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 2a + 3 = 15, what is a²?
questions.explanation: 2a = 12, so a = 6 and a² = 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If x/3 − 2 = 4, what is x?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: If 3(x + 4) = 2x + 19, what is x?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: One number is 5 more than twice another. Their sum is 41. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: Let the smaller be n: n + (2n + 5) = 41, so 3n = 36 and n = 12. The larger is 2 × 12 + 5 = 29.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Adult tickets cost ₱150 and child tickets ₱90. Twenty tickets were sold for ₱2,460. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let a be adult tickets: 150a + 90(20 − a) = 2,460, so 60a = 660 and a = 11.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 132. What is the larger one?
questions.explanation: 11 × 12 = 132, so the larger integer is 12.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Three siblings were born 2 years apart. The sum of their ages is 36. How old is the eldest?
questions.explanation: The middle child is 36 ÷ 3 = 12, so the ages are 10, 12 and 14.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Lito is 4 years younger than twice his sister's age. His sister is 15. How old is Lito?
questions.explanation: Twice 15 is 30, and 4 years younger is 26.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Three clerks can each finish an inventory alone in 6, 8 and 12 days. How long will they take working together?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 3 hours, while a drain empties it in 5 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate: 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 of the tank per hour. 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 hours.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Three painters can paint a house in 8 days. How many days would four painters take at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The job is 3 × 8 = 24 painter-days. 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A bus leaves a terminal at 60 km/h. One hour later, a car leaves the same terminal on the same road at 80 km/h. How long after leaving will the car catch up with the bus?
questions.explanation: The bus has a 60 km head start. The car gains 80 − 60 = 20 km each hour, so 60 ÷ 20 = 3 hours.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A train travels 360 km in 4.5 hours. What is its speed?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Walking at 5 km/h, how long does it take to walk 12.5 km?
questions.explanation: 12.5 ÷ 5 = 2.5 hours, or 2 hours 30 minutes.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 15. If the number 29 is removed, what is the average of the rest?
questions.explanation: The total is 8 × 15 = 120. Without 29 it is 91, and 91 ÷ 7 = 13.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Section A has 30 students with an average score of 80. Section B has 20 students with an average of 85. What is the average of all 50 students?
questions.explanation: Total: 30 × 80 + 20 × 85 = 2,400 + 1,700 = 4,100. 4,100 ÷ 50 = 82. (Averaging 80 and 85 directly would wrongly give 82.5.)

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average salary of 4 clerks is ₱20,000. One leaves, and the average of the other 3 becomes ₱19,000. What was the salary of the clerk who left?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A store buys 20 items at ₱50 each and 30 items at ₱60 each. What is the average cost per item?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₱24,000 at 5% a year for 9 months?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What principal earns ₱1,800 in simple interest in 3 years at 4% a year?
questions.explanation: Principal = interest ÷ (rate × time) = ₱1,800 ÷ 0.12 = ₱15,000.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: ₱20,000 is invested at 6% interest compounded annually. What is the amount after 2 years?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A real estate agent earns a 3% commission on a ₱2,400,000 house. How much is the commission?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An item costs ₱2,500 before VAT. How much is the 12% VAT?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Suppose income above ₱250,000 is taxed at 15%, and income up to ₱250,000 is not taxed. How much tax is due on an income of ₱330,000?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A car uses 8 liters of fuel per 100 km. How many liters does it need for 350 km?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: 45 minutes is what fraction of an hour?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How many hectares are in 1 square kilometer?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A meeting starts at 1:45 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 50 minutes. When does it end?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: How many days are there from March 28 to April 5, counting both dates?
questions.explanation: March 28 to 31 is 4 days, and April 1 to 5 is 5 days: 9 days in all.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 12 m long and 8 m wide?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A rectangle has an area of 72 m² and a width of 6 m. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Length = 72 ÷ 6 = 12 m. Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 6) = 36 m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A lot 30 m by 20 m is fenced with posts every 2.5 m all around, starting at a corner. How many posts are needed?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is 2 × (30 + 20) = 100 m. On a closed loop, 100 ÷ 2.5 = 40 posts.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm? (Use π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 1,540 cm³.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. How far does it travel in 100 turns? (Use π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: One turn = circumference = 22/7 × 70 = 220 cm. 100 turns = 22,000 cm = 220 m.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ...
questions.explanation: Each term is doubled plus 1: 31 × 2 + 1 = 63.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? 100, 95, 85, 70, 50, ...
questions.explanation: The amount subtracted grows by 5: −5, −10, −15, −20, then −25.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ...
questions.explanation: These are the prime numbers. The next prime after 13 is 17.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ...
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6: 16 + 6 = 22.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is 36 ÷ (4 + 2) × 3 − 5?
questions.explanation: Parentheses first: 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Then 6 × 3 = 18, and 18 − 5 = 13.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is (3²)³?
questions.explanation: A power of a power multiplies the exponents: 3⁶ = 729.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the greatest common factor of 72 and 108?
questions.explanation: 72 = 2 × 36 and 108 = 3 × 36, and 2 and 3 share no factor, so the GCF is 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the smallest number divisible by 4, 6 and 9?
questions.explanation: The LCM of 4, 6 and 9 is 36.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: In how many different orders can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: An office's ₱480,000 budget gives 25% to training. How much is that?

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: A price is lowered by 25% and then raised by 25%. What is the overall change?
questions.explanation: 0.75 × 1.25 = 0.9375, so the final price is 93.75% of the original: a 6.25% decrease.

questions.subject: Numerical Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between the clock hands at exactly 9:00?
questions.explanation: The hands are 3 hour-marks apart, and each mark is 30°: 3 × 30 = 90°.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Seed is to tree as egg is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is an early stage and what it grows into.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Kilogram is to mass as kilometer is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a unit and what it measures.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Library is to books as gallery is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a place and what it keeps on display.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Fish is to gills as human is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is an animal and the organ it breathes with.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Mayor is to city as governor is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a local chief executive and the unit they head.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Caterpillar is to butterfly as tadpole is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a young stage and the adult it becomes.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Painter is to canvas as sculptor is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is an artist and the material they work on.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Dentist is to teeth as optometrist is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a specialist and the part of the body they care for.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Week is to month as month is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a smaller unit of time and the larger unit it makes up.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Generous is to stingy as brave is to ___.
questions.explanation: The words are opposites.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Speedometer is to speed as odometer is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is an instrument and what it measures.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Bread is to bakery as medicine is to ___.
questions.explanation: The relationship is a product and the shop that sells it.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? A, B, D, G, K, ...
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by one: +1, +2, +3, +4, then +5. K + 5 = P.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? Z, W, T, Q, ...
questions.explanation: Each letter moves back by three: Q − 3 = N.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? ACE, BDF, CEG, ...
questions.explanation: Each letter in the group moves forward by one: A→B→C→D, C→D→E→F, E→F→G→H.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? A, E, I, M, ...
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by four: M + 4 = Q.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: What comes next? BD, EG, HJ, ...
questions.explanation: Each pair starts three letters after the last (B, E, H, K) and skips one letter inside the pair.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If ROAD is coded as URDG, how is CITY coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by three, wrapping from Z to A: C→F, I→L, T→W, Y→B.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a code, 1 = R, 2 = E, 3 = A and 4 = D. What word is 4-2-3-1?

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a code, each vowel is replaced by the next vowel (A→E, E→I, I→O, O→U, U→A) and consonants stay the same. How is TABLE written?
questions.explanation: A becomes E and E becomes I; T, B and L stay: TEBLI.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a code, A = Z, B = Y, C = X and so on (the alphabet reversed). How is CAB written?
questions.explanation: C→X, A→Z, B→Y.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: SEND is coded as 4-14-5-19: the letters' alphabet positions, written in reverse order. How is GIFT coded?
questions.explanation: G = 7, I = 9, F = 6, T = 20. In reverse order: 20-6-9-7.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: All A are B. No B are C. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.explanation: Every A is inside B, and nothing in B is C, so no A can be C.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Some officials are lawyers. No lawyers are minors. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The officials who are lawyers cannot be minors, so at least some officials are not minors.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: No managers are interns. All interns are students. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The students who are interns cannot be managers. Nothing is said about other students.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Ana says, "Ben is lying." Ben says, "Carlo is lying." Carlo says, "Ana and Ben are both lying." Who is telling the truth?
questions.explanation: If Ben tells the truth, Carlo lies, and Ana (who calls Ben a liar) lies too. Carlo's claim that both lie is then false, which fits. Any other choice leads to a contradiction.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Tomorrow is two days after Monday. What day was yesterday?
questions.explanation: Tomorrow is Wednesday, so today is Tuesday and yesterday was Monday.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: If the day after tomorrow is Saturday, what day was yesterday?
questions.explanation: The day after tomorrow is Saturday, so today is Thursday and yesterday was Wednesday.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Rule: "To be hired, an applicant must pass the exam." Which statement is true?
questions.correct: Passing the exam alone does not guarantee being hired
wrong: Applicants who fail may still be hired
Being hired has nothing to do with the exam
questions.explanation: Passing is required (necessary), but the rule does not say it is enough (sufficient).

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Ana, Ben, Carla and Dan are a teacher, a nurse, an engineer and a clerk, one each. Ben is the teacher. Ana is not the nurse or the engineer. Carla is not the clerk or the nurse. What is Dan?
questions.explanation: Carla can only be the engineer, so Ana is the clerk, leaving nurse for Dan.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Five houses stand in a row. The white house is at the left end and the green house at the right end. The yellow house is between the red and the blue houses, and the red house is left of the blue one. Which house is in the middle?
questions.explanation: The order is white, red, yellow, blue, green. Yellow is third.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: A is heavier than B. C is lighter than B. D is heavier than A. Who is the second heaviest?
questions.explanation: From heaviest: D, A, B, C.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Lea arrived before Mon. Nina arrived after Mon. Oca arrived before Lea. Who arrived third?
questions.explanation: The order is Oca, Lea, Mon, Nina.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Accounting is on the 2nd floor. HR is two floors above Accounting, and Records is directly below HR. On which floor is Records?
questions.explanation: HR is on the 4th floor, so Records, directly below, is on the 3rd.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Tina walks 5 km south and then 12 km west. How far is she from her starting point in a straight line?
questions.explanation: The path forms a right triangle: √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: You face east, turn left, and turn left again. Which direction do you face?
questions.explanation: Left from east is north; left again is west.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Town A is 10 km north of a junction and Town B is 10 km east of it. In which direction is Town B from Town A?
questions.explanation: From A you go south to reach the junction's level and east to reach B.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: From the town hall, Ella walks 3 km west, 3 km north, 3 km east and then 1 km south. Where is she now?
questions.correct: 2 km north of the town hall
wrong: 3 km north of the town hall
1 km south of the town hall
2 km west of the town hall
questions.explanation: West and east cancel out. North 3 km and south 1 km leave her 2 km north.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which does not belong with the others? Jupiter, Mars, Moon, Venus
questions.explanation: Jupiter, Mars and Venus are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which number does not belong? 2, 3, 5, 9, 11
questions.explanation: All are prime except 9, which is 3 × 3.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Which does not belong with the others? Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao, Manila
questions.explanation: Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao are the three main island groups; Manila is a city.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: A woman says of a boy, "His mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is the woman related to the boy?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of her mother is herself, so she is the boy's mother.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Rosa is Ben's sister. Ben is Carlo's father. How is Rosa related to Carlo?
questions.explanation: Rosa is the sister of Carlo's father, so she is his aunt.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: An office issued 40 permits on Monday, 55 on Tuesday, 35 on Wednesday, 60 on Thursday and 50 on Friday. What is the average per day?
questions.explanation: Total: 240 permits. 240 ÷ 5 = 48.

questions.subject: Analytical Ability
questions.question: Of 200 employees, 45% work in operations, 30% in administration and the rest in finance. How many work in finance?

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How does the Preamble of the 1987 Constitution begin?
wrong: "We, the people of the Philippine Islands"
questions.explanation: The Preamble opens with "We, the sovereign Filipino people, imploring the aid of Almighty God..."

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Article I of the 1987 Constitution is about what?
questions.explanation: Article I defines the national territory, including the archipelago and the waters around it.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under Article IV, who are natural-born citizens?
questions.correct: Citizens of the Philippines from birth, without having to perform any act to acquire or perfect citizenship
wrong: Anyone who has lived in the Philippines for at least ten continuous years
Foreigners who marry a Filipino citizen and live in the country
Anyone who passes the citizenship test and swears an oath of loyalty
questions.explanation: Natural-born citizens are Filipinos from birth who did not have to do anything to become citizens.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under Article V, how long must a person have lived in the Philippines to vote?
questions.correct: At least one year, and at least six months in the place where they will vote
wrong: At least five years in the same barangay
At least three months anywhere in the country
At least two years in the same province
questions.explanation: Article V, Section 1 sets these residence requirements for suffrage.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Party-list representatives make up what share of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 5(2) provides that party-list representatives constitute 20% of the total membership of the House.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What is the minimum age to be a Member of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: A district representative must be at least 25 years old on election day.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How long must a candidate for Senator have resided in the Philippines immediately before the election?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 3 requires residence in the Philippines for at least two years immediately preceding the election.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: When does Congress convene for its regular session each year?
questions.correct: On the fourth Monday of July
wrong: On the first Monday of June
On the third Monday of May
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 15 sets the opening of the regular session on the fourth Monday of July.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: If the President dies in office, who becomes President for the rest of the term?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 8 provides that the Vice President becomes President.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: If both the President and Vice President die, who acts as President first?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 8 names the Senate President first, then the Speaker of the House.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How long must a candidate for President have resided in the Philippines immediately before the election?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 2 requires ten years of residence immediately preceding the election.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: At what age must members of the Supreme Court retire?
questions.explanation: Justices hold office until they reach the age of 70 (Article VIII, Section 11).

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which body recommends appointees to the Judiciary, including the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: The Judicial and Bar Council prepares the lists of nominees from which the President appoints.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: The Commission on Audit is composed of whom?
wrong: Five Commissioners with a rotating head
questions.explanation: Article IX-D provides for a Chairman and two Commissioners.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Article X provides for autonomous regions in which two areas?
questions.explanation: Article X, Section 15 provides for autonomous regions in Muslim Mindanao and the Cordilleras.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What is the term of office of the Ombudsman?
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 11 sets a seven-year term without reappointment.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: To explore and develop natural resources with the State, a corporation must be at least what percent Filipino-owned?
questions.explanation: Article XII, Section 2 allows agreements with Filipino citizens or corporations at least 60% owned by Filipinos.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution is about what?
questions.explanation: Article XIII covers social justice and human rights, and creates the Commission on Human Rights.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: According to Article XVI, what are the colors of the Philippine flag?
questions.correct: Red, white and blue, with a sun and three stars
wrong: Red, yellow and blue, with a moon
Red, white and green, with a sun
questions.explanation: Article XVI, Section 1 describes the flag as red, white and blue, with a sun and three stars.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: An amendment to the Constitution is ratified in a plebiscite held within what period after it is approved?
questions.correct: Not earlier than 60 days nor later than 90 days
wrong: Not earlier than 90 days nor later than 180 days
questions.explanation: Article XVII, Section 4 sets the plebiscite between 60 and 90 days after approval.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Article II, Section 6 says the separation of Church and State shall be what?
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 6: "The separation of Church and State shall be inviolable."

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under Article II, Section 2, the Philippines renounces what as an instrument of national policy?
questions.explanation: The Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: For communication and instruction, what are the official languages of the Philippines?
questions.correct: Filipino and, unless otherwise provided by law, English
questions.explanation: Article XIV, Section 7 names Filipino and English as official languages.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How may Congress revoke a proclamation of martial law?
questions.correct: By a vote of at least a majority of all its Members, voting jointly
wrong: By a vote of two-thirds of the Senate, voting separately
By a vote of three-fourths of the House, voting separately
By a unanimous vote of all Members of both Houses
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 18 lets Congress revoke it by a majority of all its Members voting jointly.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: When can an increase in the salaries of Senators and Representatives take effect?
questions.correct: Only after the full term of all the Members who approved it has ended
wrong: Immediately after the law is signed by the President
At the start of the next fiscal year after it is approved
Only after it is approved by the people in a plebiscite
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 10 prevents members from raising their own pay during their term.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What makes up a quorum to do business in each House of Congress?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 16(2): a majority of each House constitutes a quorum.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How many norms of conduct does Section 4 of RA 6713 list?
questions.explanation: The eight norms are commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 requires prompt, courteous and adequate service to the public?
questions.explanation: Responsiveness to the public means extending prompt, courteous and adequate service.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 includes promoting the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology?
questions.explanation: Nationalism and patriotism includes loyalty to the Republic and promoting local goods and technology.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 includes upholding civilian supremacy over the military?
questions.explanation: Commitment to democracy includes public accountability and civilian supremacy over the military.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How many articles does the Universal Declaration of Human Rights have?
questions.explanation: The UDHR has 30 articles.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 11166 of 2018 is known as what law?
questions.correct: Philippine HIV and AIDS Policy Act
questions.explanation: RA 11166 strengthens the national response to HIV and protects people living with HIV from discrimination.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What does Republic Act No. 11596 of 2021 prohibit?
questions.explanation: RA 11596 declares child marriage illegal and penalizes those who facilitate it.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 11861 of 2022 expanded the benefits of which group?
questions.explanation: RA 11861 is the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 7877 of 1995 is known as what law?
questions.explanation: RA 7877 penalizes sexual harassment in work, education and training settings.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 10931 provides free tuition in which schools?
questions.correct: State universities and colleges and local universities and colleges
wrong: Private colleges and universities that join the program
Public elementary and high schools only
Technical schools run by private companies
questions.explanation: RA 10931, the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act of 2017, provides free tuition in SUCs and LUCs.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which two treaties, adopted by the UN in 1966, form the International Bill of Human Rights together with the UDHR?
wrong: The Paris Agreement and the Kyoto Protocol
questions.explanation: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights were adopted in 1966.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 11930 of 2022 protects children against what?
questions.explanation: RA 11930 is the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: The right to work and the right to education belong to which group of rights?
questions.explanation: These are covered by the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under RA 10754, what do persons with disability receive on covered goods and services?
questions.correct: A 20% discount and exemption from VAT
questions.explanation: RA 10754 of 2016 gives PWDs a 20% discount and VAT exemption on covered goods and services.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Freedom of speech and the right to vote belong to which group of rights?
questions.explanation: These are covered by the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which law, passed in 1992, established the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS)?
questions.explanation: RA 7586 created NIPAS; RA 11038 of 2018 later expanded it.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 9512 of 2008 promotes what?
questions.correct: Environmental awareness and education in schools
questions.explanation: RA 9512, the Environmental Awareness and Education Act of 2008, integrates environmental education in the curriculum.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 10771 of 2016 is known as what law?
questions.explanation: RA 10771 provides incentives for businesses that create green jobs.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 11898 of 2022 makes large companies responsible for recovering what?
questions.explanation: RA 11898, the Extended Producer Responsibility Act, requires large enterprises to recover or offset their plastic packaging waste.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: The Kyoto Protocol of 1997 set binding targets for what?
questions.correct: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions in developed countries
wrong: Protecting whales and other marine mammals
Ending all deforestation by the year 2000
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol committed developed countries to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: World Environment Day is observed every year on what date?
questions.explanation: The United Nations observes World Environment Day on June 5.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What does the ozone layer do?
questions.correct: It absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays
wrong: It traps heat near the ground
questions.explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere filters out most harmful UV radiation.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: In the Philippines, La Niña is usually associated with what?
questions.explanation: La Niña tends to bring above-normal rainfall, while El Niño brings below-normal rainfall.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: How do mangrove forests help coastal communities?
questions.correct: They protect the coast from storm surges and erosion
questions.explanation: Mangroves reduce wave energy, hold soil together and shelter young fish.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which of these is biodegradable waste?
questions.explanation: Biodegradable waste breaks down naturally; peelings can be composted.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What is a storm surge?
questions.correct: An abnormal rise of seawater pushed onshore by a storm's strong winds
wrong: Heavy rain that makes rivers overflow their banks
A sudden earthquake under the sea that shakes the coast
A strong gust of wind that comes right after a storm
questions.explanation: Storm surges are caused by strong winds and low pressure pushing seawater inland.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: In PAGASA's rainfall warning system, which color is the most serious?
questions.explanation: Yellow, orange and red warnings increase in seriousness; red calls for evacuation in flood-prone areas.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: You are at the beach after a strong earthquake and the sea suddenly pulls back. What should you do?
wrong: Walk out to look at the exposed seabed
Wait for an announcement on the beach
questions.explanation: A sudden drop in sea level is a natural tsunami warning sign.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: An emergency "go bag" should hold supplies for at least how long?
questions.explanation: Go bags are commonly prepared to last at least 72 hours, until help arrives.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which month is National Disaster Resilience Month in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Executive Order No. 29, s. 2017 declared July as National Disaster Resilience Month.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 9514 of 2008 is known as what?
questions.explanation: RA 9514 is the Fire Code of the Philippines, enforced by the Bureau of Fire Protection.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under RA 10121, which department heads disaster response as a vice-chair of the NDRRMC?
questions.correct: Department of Social Welfare and Development
wrong: Department of Public Works and Highways
questions.explanation: The DSWD Secretary is vice-chair for disaster response.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: The 1996 Final Peace Agreement was signed between the government and which group?
questions.explanation: The 1996 Final Peace Agreement was signed with the MNLF; the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement was with the MILF.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: In what year was the Bangsamoro Organic Law ratified in a plebiscite?
questions.explanation: The plebiscites were held in January and February 2019.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which month is National Peace Consciousness Month in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Proclamation No. 675, s. 2004 declared September as National Peace Consciousness Month.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Under international humanitarian law, what does the principle of distinction require?
questions.correct: That parties to a conflict distinguish between civilians and combatants
wrong: That countries keep their borders closed
questions.explanation: Attacks may be directed only at combatants and military targets, never at civilians.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Which law was the original Anti-Red Tape Act, later amended by RA 11032?
questions.explanation: RA 9485 was the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007; RA 11032 expanded it in 2018.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 10149 of 2011 governs which kind of entities?
wrong: Local government units such as provinces and cities
Private hospitals and health maintenance organizations
questions.explanation: RA 10149, the GOCC Governance Act, created the Governance Commission for GOCCs.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 10175 of 2012 is known as what law?
questions.explanation: RA 10175 defines and penalizes cybercrimes such as hacking and online fraud.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: What is the passing rating in the Civil Service Examination?
questions.explanation: Examinees need a general rating of at least 80 to pass.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Sub-Professional eligibility is appropriate for which positions?
questions.correct: First-level positions, such as clerical and trade positions
questions.explanation: Sub-Professional eligibility covers first-level positions; Professional eligibility covers first- and second-level positions.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Presidential Decree No. 907 grants civil service eligibility to whom?
questions.explanation: PD 907 grants civil service eligibility to graduates with Latin honors such as cum laude.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 10667 of 2015 promotes what?
questions.explanation: RA 10667, the Philippine Competition Act, prohibits anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant position.

questions.subject: General Information
questions.question: Republic Act No. 11223 of 2019 is known as what law?
wrong: Magna Carta of Public Health Workers
questions.explanation: RA 11223 enrolls all Filipinos in the National Health Insurance Program.
